chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, from his father, from Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:
"I do not mind whether it was urine that touched me or water, so long as I do not know."

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: If blood reaches his garment and its amount is the size of the full dirham, which was struck from one dirham and a third, then washing it is obligatory upon him, and salat (prayer) in it is not permissible for him. But if its amount is less than that, and it is like a chickpea, a fingernail, or the like, then salat (prayer) in it before washing it is permissible for him, though washing it for salat (prayer) in it is better. Except if it is menstrual blood, for salat (prayer) is not permissible in a small or large amount of it, and washing the garment from it is obligatory, even if its amount is as small as the head of a needle.

key_terms.الدِّرْهَمِ الْوَافِي: the full dirham; the legal size threshold used for blood stains
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer); the act of worship whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.بَوْلٌ: urine; a source of ritual impurity mentioned in the statement of uncertainty
key_terms.دَمٌ: blood; the impurity discussed regarding its amount on clothing
key_terms.دَمَ حَيْضٍ: menstrual blood; a category of blood treated more strictly in this ruling
key_terms.غَسْلُهُ: washing it; the required act of purification for the garment
key_terms.مَاءٌ: water; contrasted with urine in a case of not knowing what touched one

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in clothing stained with a small amount of blood?
ai.summary: This report addresses uncertainty regarding impurity and the legal rulings on blood on clothing for salat (prayer). It distinguishes between small and larger amounts of blood, while making an exception for menstrual blood, which must always be washed and cannot be overlooked in salat (prayer).
